subject: Maths
central_question: How can patterns, digits, operations, estimates, and games reveal surprising properties of numbers?
in_scope_units: 3.3 Patterns of Numbers on the Number Line
3.10 An Unsolved Mystery — the Collatz Conjecture
banned_topics: Claiming the Collatz conjecture is proved
Algebraic sequence formulae beyond the chapter

known_pitfalls.claim: A large value is automatically a supercell.
known_pitfalls.correction: It must be larger than every relevant neighbouring cell.

known_pitfalls.claim: Kaprekar's routine works normally when all four digits are identical.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter uses at least two distinct digits; identical digits lead to 0000.

recommended_example_progression: Identify neighbours and supercells in Sections 3.1–3.2.
Use digit sums and palindromes in Sections 3.4–3.5.
Use estimation and Games 21 and 99 in Sections 3.11–3.12.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: Use the Figure it Out, Math Talk, Collatz, estimation, and game challenges across Sections 3.1–3.12.
